req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for subsequent DELETE calls on the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states DELETE /tasks/{task_id} is idempotent: first call returns 204, subsequent calls return 404. We need: (1) positive case — first DELETE returns 204 No Content; (2) state-transition case — second DELETE on same id returns 404; (3) negative/boundary case — DELETE on a never-existing id returns 404 immediately. We use pre-loaded rows (ids 1-20) and an in-memory SQLite override to keep tests isolated and deterministic. Each test overrides get_db to use a fresh in-memory DB seeded with the fixture rows, ensuring idempotency across test runs. Assertions use exact status codes (204, 404) to catch constant-mutation operators. We also assert the 404 detail message content to catch string-mutation operators.

preconditions: Task with id=5 exists in the database (pre-loaded fixture row)
FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: Send DELETE /tasks/5 to the in-process TestClient
trace: R-TASK-028: first DELETE on existing task_id must return 2xx (204)
tests.executable:
import os
os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite://')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base
from app.main import app
from app import models
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

engine_mem = create_engine('sqlite://', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
SessionMem = sessionmaker(bind=engine_mem)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine_mem)

db_seed = SessionMem()
db_seed.add(models.Task(id=5, title='Write project report', description='Signal cascade', completed=False))
db_seed.commit()
db_seed.close()

def override_get_db():
    db = SessionMem()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

from app.database import get_db
app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_existing_task_returns_204():
    r = client.delete('/tasks/5')
    assert r.status_code == 204
    assert r.content == b''

test_delete_existing_task_returns_204()
app.dependency_overrides.clear()

from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.database import Base, get_db
from app.main import app
from app import models
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

engine_mem5 = create_engine('sqlite://', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
SessionMem5 = sessionmaker(bind=engine_mem5)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine_mem5)

db_seed5 = SessionMem5()
db_seed5.add(models.Task(id=2, title='Book flight tickets', description='Delta willow', completed=True))
db_seed5.add(models.Task(id=3, title='Submit expense report', description='Pulse willow', completed=True))
db_seed5.commit()
db_seed5.close()

def override_get_db5():
    db = SessionMem5()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db5
client5 = TestClient(app)

def test_delete_does_not_affect_other_tasks():
    r1 = client5.delete('/tasks/2')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client5.get('/tasks/3')
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    body = r2.json()
    assert body['id'] == 3
    assert body['title'] == 'Submit expense report'
    r3 = client5.delete('/tasks/2')
    assert r3.status_code == 404

test_delete_does_not_affect_other_tasks()
app.dependency_overrides.clear()
